events.title: TailLoRA idea
events.content: TailLoRA gives more rank to the blocks whose gradient norm on tail-class samples is largest: total budget 96 ranks over 12 blocks, reallocated every 2 epochs. The idea came from a chat with Tomás, not from AdaLoRA's SVD pruning.
One ViT-B/16 run on CIFAR-100-LT (30 epochs) takes about 41 minutes on a single A100-40GB, so 5 seeds of one config cost roughly 3.5 GPU-hours.
TailLoRA v1 (budget 96, realloc every 2 epochs, split v3, seed 0): 70.8% overall and 51.9% few-shot, above full fine-tuning (70.4%) with only 0.29M trainable parameters.

AdaLoRA (Zhang et al., ICLR 2023) parametrises the update as P Λ Q and prunes singular values by a smoothed sensitivity score; typical setting is initial rank 12 going down to a target of 8, with an orthogonality regulariser of weight 0.1.

events.title: Router collapse in CMoE
events.content: Router collapse in CMoE: with softmax temperature 1.0 and no load-balancing loss, 3 of the 4 experts received less than 2% of the samples by epoch 10, and accuracy looked fine only because the surviving expert acted like plain LoRA. The usage entropy was 0.62 nats (maximum is 1.386). Fix: auxiliary load-balance loss with weight 0.01 and temperature 0.5, which brings the entropy back to 1.31 nats. A weight of 0.1 gives 1.38 nats but costs accuracy (70.1 instead of 70.9). I found it by logging per-expert token counts every epoch, not by looking at the loss curve.
MoLE-style baseline (4 experts with r=4, token-level router, split v3, seed 0): 70.2% overall and 50.9% few-shot, compared to CMoE with the frequency router at 70.9% / 52.5%.

events.title: Load-balance weight sweep
events.content: Load-balance loss weight sweep for CMoE (4 × r=4, split v3, seed 0): 0.001 gives entropy 0.84 and 70.5%, 0.01 gives entropy 1.31 and 70.9%, 0.1 gives entropy 1.38 and 70.1%. Keep 0.01.
